skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

I removed each `admit()` and attempted real proofs; here are the **exact** remaining errors and why each is a deferred-ghost-token / dependency-spec-minimality blocker, not a proof-skill gap.
45. 
46. #### 1. `ensure_pt` (identity_map.rs:533) — blocked by `bump_view(self).inv()`
47.

51.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:555:9
52. 556 | |  .alloc_as::<[PteWord; PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH]>()
53. 350 |    requires bump_view(self).inv(),   (bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:350)
54.     |             --------------------- failed precondition
55. ```
56. `bump_view` is a parameter-free `uninterp spec fn` (bump_allocator `lib.spec.rs`) with **no establishing lemma and no `type_invariant`** anywhere in the tree:
57. ```
58. $ grep -rn "bump_view" src --include=*.rs | grep -iE "ensures|inv\(\)|broadcast|axiom"   → (none)
59. $ grep -rn "type_invariant" src/libs/bump_allocator/                                       → (none)
60. ```
61. No caller can prove `inv()` for the concrete `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR` static — this is the bump allocator's own deferred ghost token. The alloc path is unavoidable in `ensure_pt`, so this single obligation makes the function unprovable in-body.
62. 
63. #### 2. `ensure_pte` (identity_map.rs:627) — blocked by `mapped.contains` postcondition
64. 
65. ```
66. error: precondition not satisfied         --> identity_map.rs:637:40   (pt.read index — solvable via into_raw)
67. error: postcondition not satisfied        --> identity_map.rs:624:13
68.     |  Ok  => identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr@))
69.     |  Err => !identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr@))
70. ```
71. `Table::write` (table.rs:246) is deliberately **contents-free** (`external_body`; a contents postcondition would be UNSOUND per its TCB note), and `identity_map_view()` is a parameter-free `uninterp` whose value is identical pre/post a concrete page-table write. There is **no spec link** from a concrete PTE write to global-view membership, so the `mapped.contains` postcondition is underivable.
72. 
73. #### 3. `identity_map_page` (identity_map.rs:718) — blocked by `accessible` postcondition
74. 
75. ```
76. error: postcondition not satisfied        --> identity_map.rs:712:13   (x3 arms)
77.     |  identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@)   /   !accessible(...)
78. ```
79. Same root cause: no spec relates the `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` atomic load + sub-call composition to the parameter-free `identity_map_view()`.
80. 
81. #### Additional limitation hit
82. `use_type_invariant(pde_idx)` on arch's `TableIndex` raises **`Verus Internal Error: missing type invariant function`** (cross-crate; documented at `phys.rs:137-156` and `verus-unsupported.md`). The supported workaround `TableIndex::into_raw()` is what I used above — it confirms the index bounds are *not* the wall; the ghost-token obligations are.
83. 
84. #### Why this is a guidance request, not a skill gap
85. Every analogous function in the completed sibling module `mm::phys` that references the parameter-free `phys_view()` (`frame::alloc/book/instance`, `kframe::new`) is `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` + listed in `tcb-allowed.md`, with the view-attachment lemmas (`lemma_manager_attached`) left as deferred axioms. Notably, `kframe::new` is TCB-listed **specifically because** it calls `identity_map_page` and needs the unrealized `mm::virt` token. The spec phase placed these three functions in-scope with `admit()` anticipating that same token would later be realized.
86. 
87. **Decision needed:** to reach `admit=0` for the exec trio, one of the following — both outside this in-body, fixed-signature module task — must happen:
88. - **(a)** Realize the `mm::virt` identity-map ghost token: a `bump_view(...).inv()` attachment lemma for `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR`, plus spec links from `Table::write`/atomic loads to `identity_map_view()`. This is cross-cutting infra spanning `bump_allocator`, `arch::paging`, and `mm::virt`.
89. - **(b)** Reclassify the three exec functions as TCB `external_body` (mirroring their `mm::phys` analogues) — which requires adding them to `tcb-allowed.md`, currently **forbidden** by the proving rules.
90. 
91. I have left the three `proof! { admit(); }` lines in place so the module stays green (9 verified, 0 errors) and the build passes, pending your direction on (a) vs (b).
92.
